Monica / team —

Quick ops feasibility notes:

1) Inventory and pool sizing
- Baseline: 4 gpus (A100/80GB equiv) in us-west-2 across 2 AZs (2/2) recommended for redundancy.
- Burst target: scale to 12 gpus in the pool. To support that without cold-start latency we should reserve a warm pool of 4 nodes (kept in spun-up state but with minimal processes) and allow the autoscaler to spin additional nodes as needed.

2) Autoscale & pre-warm windows
- Autoscale triggers: we recommend token-per-second thresholds + queue latency metrics.
- Pre-warm approach: schedule a 10-minute pre-warm window for predictable nightly jobs; for unpredictable spikes we can use on-demand burst with warm pool + aggressive instance launch (target 3–5 min to add nodes).
- Warm pool cost tradeoff: keeping 4 warm nodes increases baseline cost ~18% but reduces cold-start penalties to under 30s for new sessions.

3) Quota & provisioning requests
- We'll need to request additional GPU quota per AZ: request 8 extra GPUs in us-west-2 and 6 in eu-west-1 as a starting point. I'll draft the quota ticket and estimated lead times (usually 48–72 hours).

4) Networking / private deployment notes
- For private VPC attachments: ensure Acuity's NAT gateways support egress for model container updates and metrics. If they want air-gapped image syncs we need an S3 mirroring plan (call this out in the SOW).
- Cross-region KV cache consistency: for EU fallback, we'll prefer warm, region-local KV caches and route EU traffic to eu-west-1 to preserve residency. That requires routing policies in the control plane (we have that, will configure per-MAP).

5) Attachments I will bring to kickoff
- pool_capacity_estimates.xlsx (high-level numbers per AZ)
- warm_pool-costing.pdf (cost tradeoff table)

Action items for kickoff prep:
- Chloe: confirm kickoff invite and include Acuity infra lead + procurement.
- Monica: prepare SOW redlines; include data-residency clause for EU logs.
- Ops (me): raise quota ticket and attach pool_capacity_estimates.xlsx.

I'll be on the kickoff and can present the ops constraints.

—Karthik
